newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Lebed accused of plotting, tension grows.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Lebed accused of plotting, tension grows.

text.p: Russia's interior minister accused security tsar Alexander Lebed on Wednesday of plotting to take power by force while President Boris Yeltsin is out of the Kremlin awaiting heart surgery.

Minutes after General Anatoly Kulikov's attack, the fiercest blow in a Kremlin power struggle, a Russian news agency said Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin had summoned Kulikov and his defence and intelligence chiefs to an urgent meeting.

Lebed denied the accusations and said he would press charges against Kulikov. Yeltsin himself kept out of the fray but doctors dismissed rumours that he had a blood problem and said his heart operation would go ahead as scheduled in mid-November.
"(Lebed) has decided to move ahead using force instead of waiting for the next presidential poll," Kulikov, Lebed's bitter political rival, told a news conference.
"The question is what awaits Russia if Lebed comes to power through a creeping coup."
Kulikov said Chernomyrdin had documents proving the plot but Lebed denied any wrong-doing and told Interfax news agency: "I intend to sue Anatoly Kulikov."
The row marked a sharp deterioration in a power struggle which has intensified since Yeltsin announced on September 5 that he would need a heart operation.

Sergei Mironov, head of the Kremlin medical centre, indicated Yeltsin had had a blood problem at some stage. But he made clear it had cleared up and he rallied behind presidential spokesmen by striking an optimistic note.
"The operation on President Boris Yeltsin's heart will be carried out as planned in the middle of November," Mironov told Interfax. "There are no grounds for saying that Boris Yeltsin is inoperable."

Yeltsin met President Alexander Lukashenko of Belarus at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow. But he moved slowly, his eyes were puffy and his voice was barely audible in brief television footage of the 40-minute meeting.
Yeltsin dropped out of public view shortly before he was re-elected on July 3. He had two heart attacks last year and one surgeon says he may have had a third this summer.

He has handed some of his duties to Chernomyrdin, but many officials have been jostling for position in a struggle which has become more overt in the past week. Yeltsin appealed for an end to the bickering on Tuesday.
Lebed, a 46-year-old former paratroop commander, blamed Kulikov on Tuesday for allowing fighting to rage on in breakaway Chechnya until a peace deal was signed by Lebed on August 31.
Kulikov hit back by saying the peace deal, under which Russian troops are being withdrawn from Chechnya, amounts to capitulation by Moscow.

He stepped up his charges on Wednesday by saying Lebed was planning to set up an elite "legion" -- a force designed to fight "civil unrest". Lebed's aide said all plans for a new mobile force had been discussed with Kulikov and others.

RIA news agency said Chernomyrdin had summoned Kulikov, Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and his intelligence chief to an urgent meeting but gave no details. It was not clear if Lebed had also been invited to attend.

The drama overshadowed a visit to Moscow by U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry intended to persuade Russian parliament to ratify the START-2 treaty which would slash the number of strategic nuclear warheads to a third of Cold War levels.
Rodionov said after talks with Perry that he hoped parliament would ratify the treaty.
